hypothesis: If the claim holds, measured hard-shelled eggs will always have a longer axis than breadth (prolate), with none being oblate.
pass_criterion: Among at least 1000 measured eggs from at least 100 species, 100% have length/breadth > 1.0 (within measurement error of 2%) and none are oblate.
fail_criterion: Any species' mean length/breadth is < 0.98, or more than 0.5% of eggs measured are oblate.
interpretation: 'Prolate spheroid, never oblate' is read as length exceeding maximum breadth in a solid of revolution. Nearly spherical eggs (owls) are allowed if the ratio is >= 1.
no_dataset_reason: I could not verify a specific public egg-shape dataset with a confirmed DOI or landing page. A search did not find the Stoddard et al. 2017 data deposit, and I will not name an unverified identifier.
